title: Credential reset — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of credential-reset-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema, so this file is normative and hand-checked, never machine-validated.

resetCredentialInput.description:
SIX FIELDS. THIS ROUTE CARRIES TWO DIFFERENT PRINCIPALS' LOGIN IDENTIFIERS AND BOTH NOW SAY WHOSE THEY ARE — `target_identifier` for the account being reset, `reauth_identifier` for the operator performing the reset.

RENAMED 2026-09-05, AND UNTIL THIS CHANGE THE ROUTE COULD NOT BE BUILT. Both this contract and confirmation-v1 called their field `identifier`, each coherently within its own document: confirmation-v1's is THE CALLER'S OWN and Core must assert the verified credential belongs to the calling principal; this one's is THE TARGET'S, verified against the named principal. The request carries one field and needed two meanings. Traced through the shipped code the consequence was total: splitConfirmedRequest strips `identifier` as a confirmation field, so the gate would consume the TARGET's identifier as the CALLER's, the caller-identity assertion could never hold, and `reauth_derived_value` — the operator's password salted with the OPERATOR's identifier — could not match the target's stored verifier either. BOTH HALVES FAIL AND THE ROUTE RETURNS forbidden ON EVERY WELL-FORMED REQUEST, PERMANENTLY, with no path around the gate because the permission is critical.

IT WAS FOUND BY IMPLEMENTING THE INTERSECTION, NOT BY READING EITHER DOCUMENT. Each contract is internally correct; the contradiction exists only where they meet. See contract.yaml -> theTwoIdentifiers.

FIVE FIELDS BECAME SIX AND THE ABSENCES ARE STILL THE DESIGN. CORRECTED 2026-09-05: this read 'ONE FIELD... NO email, identifier or search field' — written before CR-5 added `identifier` and before confirmation-v1 added the two confirmation fields, and never updated. IT CONTRADICTED ITS OWN `required` LIST. WHAT THE ORIGINAL OBJECTION WAS REALLY ABOUT SURVIVES INTACT: there is no route that FINDS a principal by email. `principal_id` finds it; `identifier` is verified against it and is required only because it is the KDF salt (CR-5). A lookup BY identifier remains impossible, so credential-store.ts's keyed-hash property holds. STILL ABSENT, AND EACH IS A DECISION: no operator-chosen password — 0017's basis is that entropy protects these accounts, so a human-chosen value expires that decision; no organization_id — the reset is a control-plane operation and naming a tenant would not scope it; no 'notify' or 'reason' field — the reason belongs in the audit record, which Core writes.

principal_id.description:
The principal whose credential is replaced. THIS IS HOW THE TARGET IS FOUND — `target_identifier` below is verified against it and is never an index into anything.

CR-3 IS CLOSED, CORRECTED 2026-09-05. This previously said no route in any Dudo contract produces a principal_id, so the route was unusable until one existed. `platform.organizations.members.resolve` produces one and is committed at 5cc424b. The gap was real when written and is not any more; it is corrected rather than deleted because a reader meeting the old sentence would have concluded this route could not be called at all.

target_identifier.description:
RENAMED FROM `identifier` ON 2026-09-05. It is the TARGET's, and on a request that also carries the operator's own it must say so. IT IS AN ORDINARY BODY FIELD, NOT A CONFIRMATION FIELD, WHICH MEANS IT IS NO LONGER STRIPPED BEFORE THE BINDING AND IS THEREFORE COVERED BY IT — see contract.yaml -> theTwoIdentifiers.theBindingConsequence. That is intended: the human confirms a reset for a NAMED account, and the machinery should refuse a submission that changed which account.

CANONICAL DEFINITION: urn:dudo:schema:account-identifier:1#/$defs/accountIdentifier. This is a restatement, character-identical by obligation, restated rather than $ref'd because no URN resolver exists (AS1).

PATTERN CORRECTED 2026-09-05, AND THE ASYMMETRY IT REMOVED HAD CR-5's OWN SHAPE. It was ^[!-?A-~]*@[!-?A-~]*$ — printable ASCII with '@' removed from the classes — which requires EXACTLY ONE '@'. organization-onboarding-v1 was corrected to at-least-one first, matching credential-store.ts, which never counts. FOR AN INTERVAL THIS CONTRACT THEREFORE REFUSED AN IDENTIFIER THAT ONBOARDING ACCEPTED: an account with a quoted local part containing '@' (legal under RFC 5321) could be created and could never have its credential reset. Nothing executes JSON Schema here, so it was an instruction to a person rather than a live defect — and it would have become live at the moment someone implemented validation from these documents, which is exactly how CR-5 was found. AN OPERATION THAT SILENTLY STRANDS THE ACCOUNT IT EXISTS TO RESCUE IS THIS CONTRACT'S CHARACTERISTIC FAILURE, and this was a second instance of it arriving through a pattern rather than through a rule.

THE TARGET'S LOGIN IDENTIFIER, SUPPLIED BY THE OPERATOR. ADDED 2026-09-05 AND FORCED BY ARITHMETIC — see CR-5. It is NOT a lookup key: Core computes HMAC-SHA-256(IDENTITY_LOOKUP_KEY, normalize(identifier)) and requires it to equal the stored identifier_hash for the named principal, and a mismatch returns the same argument-free 404 as an unknown principal. IT IS REQUIRED BECAUSE THE KDF SALT IS THE NORMALISED IDENTIFIER AND NOBODY ELSE HAS IT: the console has never seen it, the server stores only its keyed hash and so genuinely cannot recover it, and the target is not present to derive. Without it, a reset would write a verifier the target could never reproduce at login and would permanently brick the account it was meant to rescue. THE ORIGINAL RULING FORBADE ANY IDENTIFIER FIELD, and what that objection was really about — a route that finds a principal BY email, which is a platform-wide account-existence oracle — remains impossible here.

derived_value.description: 32 bytes, base64url. REQUIRED since docs/decisions/0026 closed ON-5/CR-5 as OPTION B — corrected 2026-09-05, having previously read 'PRESENT ONLY IF... Declared optional pending that decision' while sitting in the `required` list. The admin console generates a high-entropy password from a CSPRNG, derives PBKDF2-SHA256(NFC(password), salt = normalize(target_identifier), 600000, 32 bytes), and sends only this; the server hashes it again at 10,000 and stores that. NOTE WHICH IDENTIFIER SALTS THIS VALUE: the TARGET's, because this is the credential the TARGET will log in with. `reauth_derived_value` on the same request is salted with the OPERATOR's — two derivations, two salts, on one request, and confusing them is the defect the 2026-09-05 rename exists to make impossible. THE PASSWORD ITSELF NEVER REACHES THE SERVER, which is why it cannot appear in the response either. THE SALT COMPLICATION THAT ALMOST BROKE THIS ROUTE IS RESOLVED BY THE `target_identifier` FIELD ABOVE: the salt is the TARGET's normalised identifier, which the console has never seen and the server cannot recover from a keyed hash, so without it a reset would have written a verifier the target could never reproduce at login — a silent, permanent lockout of the account the operation exists to recover.

resetWarning.description: A CLOSED SET OF STABLE TOKENS, never free text, so a console can render each specifically and qa-agent can assert them. Both report a BOUNDED, DELIBERATE incompleteness in a security operation — the 50-session cap and the 10-Organization audit cap — and both exist because the alternative to a cap is one reset consuming the platform's entire daily write budget.

resetCredentialOutput.$comment: REMOVED 2026-09-05: a plaintext `new_password`, which was in `required`. No tombstone property is left behind — a placeholder in `properties` would be a permitted optional field under additionalProperties:false, which is the same defect one size smaller.
resetCredentialOutput.description: NO CREDENTIAL APPEARS IN THIS RESPONSE. CORRECTED 2026-09-05: this required a plaintext `new_password` while the same file required `derived_value` as INPUT — so the route demanded that the console derive the password AND that the server return a password it has no way to know. Under docs/decisions/0026 option B the console generates and derives; the server stores a hash of a hash and never holds plaintext. THE CONSOLE ALREADY HOLDS THE ONLY COPY, so the value never needed to make the round trip. Cache-Control: no-store still applies.

principal_id.description: Echoed so a console can confirm which account it just took over. It carries nothing the caller did not send.

sessions_revoked.description: How many live sessions were ended. ZERO IS AN ORDINARY AND COMMON ANSWER — the target simply was not logged in — and a console must not present it as a failure. A NON-ZERO VALUE IS THE OPERATIONALLY INTERESTING ONE: it means someone was actively using that account at the moment it was taken over, which is precisely what an operator resetting a suspected-compromised account needs to see.

warnings.description: EMPTY ON A COMPLETE OPERATION. A non-empty array means part of a SECURITY operation did not complete — sessions survive, or an Organization's copy of the trail is missing — and a console that renders it as an ordinary success has hidden the one thing an operator needed to act on.
